Everyone’s talking about this “$360K” Polymarket bot built with Claude. So we looked at what’s actually inside.

The story going viral: a marketer says he quit his job and made $360K in one month on Polymarket, using Claude as the brain of his trading system. That claim hasn’t been independently verified. But the way the system is built is real, and you can set up your own to test ideas.

Here’s how it works:

🧠 Claude is the brain. It reads the news, compares the market odds and makes the call.
🐟 MiroFish is the simulator. It’s a free, open-source tool that creates hundreds of AI “people” and plays out how they might react to the news.
🙋 You’re the decider. You paper trade first and only consider real money if the system proves itself.

The idea is simple: if the simulated crowd and the market odds disagree, there might be something worth looking at. Most of the time, the honest answer is “no trade”, and that’s the system working.

What people don’t tell you:

MiroFish wasn’t built for trading, and its makers haven’t published accuracy results.
AI crowds can swing to extremes faster than real people.
Running lots of simulations costs money in API calls.
Never copy someone else’s “winning bot” or trades.

Track at least 20 calls on paper. If it doesn’t beat the market odds, it’s not an edge.
